text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The oil deal with Russia to develop Qurna oilfield will be implemented once approved by the governments of the two countries.
- Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf returns to Baghdad.
- Iraq says U.N. trade sanctions worst violation of human rights.
- Guerrillas of Kurdish rebel leader Jalal Talabani battle Kurdish Islamists in northern Iraq.
- Turkey draws up plan to develop its southeast.
- Tunisian paper says Washington and allies set Kuwaiti oilfields on fire during the 1991 Gulf war.
- Washington fails to persuade U.N. Security Council members to issue a statement condemning Iraq for sending a pilgrim plane to Saudi Arabia.
- Ankara is prepared to enter military dialogue with Greece.
- European Union member countries recall their ambassadors from Tehran and suspend their critical dialogue with the regime there.
(The above were also carried by JUMHOURIYA and AL-IRAQ)
- Editorial says Iraq's decision to send a pilgrim plane to Saudi Arabia boosted Washington's isolation in the world.
- Article on conspiracies hatched by Washington to undermine peace efforts in northern Iraq.
- Article expounds the strategic significance of Iraq to the security of the countries in the region.
